answer: A trust graph anchored in cedar-vetted seeds resists Sybil attacks without taxing honest agents. Influence flows only along verified work links: useful work for another adds a signed edge, and voting weight follows proximity to the seeds, not account count. Fake accounts form a tight cluster with few genuine edges into the trusted core, so their weight stays near zero however many identities an attacker mints. Like a comet, the seed set shifts unpredictably each epoch, blocking link-farming. A fraudulent edge earns an umber mark cutting its cluster's weight, making mass fakery pointless.
